venue.name: Ecosummer Expeditions
venue.description: Ecosummer Expeditions is a guided sea kayaking outfitter based at a private beach at 1584 Bauza Creek Road in Telegraph Cove, on north Vancouver Island. It runs a 4 day, 3 night kayaking basecamp at Warden Beach beside the Robson Bight Ecological Reserve, a one day water taxi assisted kayak tour to the boundary of the same reserve, and an 8 day guided hike of the West Coast Trail. The kayaking trips take children from 8 or 9 years old depending on the trip, and the site says group discounts are available but never publishes a group rate. Everything runs outdoors in summer and involves a boat transfer from Telegraph Cove.
venue.address: 1584 Bauza Creek Road, Telegraph Cove, BC, Canada, V0N 3J0

facility_notes.washrooms: Robson bight basecamp is equipped with a double composting Phoenix toilet system.
facility_notes.bus_parking: Parking is free at our base for our 4 night journey to Robson Bight Basecamp.

restrictions: Minors (under 19) will require a parent/guardian signature for our waiver
We observe whales and other wildlife from a safe viewing distance, respecting international law that prohibits approaching marine mammals within 100 metres.
venue.seasonal_notes: The Robson Bight Basecamp departures listed run from mid July to early September. The Robson Bight Day Tour season is July 1 to September 10. The site says northern resident orcas transit the reserve daily from around July 15 until September 15.

programs.name: 4-Day Robson Bight Basecamp
programs.description: A 4 day, 3 night guided sea kayaking trip from a tented basecamp at Warden Beach, on the western boundary of the Robson Bight Ecological Reserve. The published rate is $1950.00 per youth aged 8 to 16 and $2050.00 per adult aged 16 and over, both plus 5 percent GST. The rate covers the round trip water taxi from Telegraph Cove, all kayaking and camping gear, tents with raised beds, sleeping bags and pillows, every meal from lunch on day one to breakfast on day four, and a 3 hour whale watching trip on the final day. Groups meet at the private beach at 1584 Bauza Creek Road at 9:30 am and the water taxi leaves at 10:00 am. Parking at the base is included. Maximum group size is 12 participants with at least two guides. The site says to ask about group discounts but does not publish one.
programs.what_children_do: Ride a water taxi half an hour from Telegraph Cove out to a beach camp, then sleep three nights in a tent on a raised bed under old growth forest. Each full day is four to six hours in a double kayak on Johnstone Strait watching for orcas, humpbacks, sea lions and eagles, with breaks for a picnic lunch. Between paddles there are rainforest and waterfall hikes, meals at the camp kitchen and a fire on the pebble beach.
programs.our_note: This is a four day wilderness camping trip rather than a day out. The youngest they take is eight, everyone sleeps in tents with a composting toilet and outdoor propane showers, and once the water taxi leaves there is no easy way off the beach until day four. If you are pricing it for a group, ask about the group discount they mention on the home page but never put a number on.
programs.practical_summary: Meals, kayaks, gear, tents and the boat transfer are all included, the camp has a composting toilet and hot showers, and parking at the Telegraph Cove base is free. Nothing is published about a school or daycare rate, how many adults have to come, or how big the deposit is, so plan on a call before you commit.
programs.extra_fees_note: Water shoes or booties, transportation to and from Telegraph Cove, overnight accommodations before or after the tour and gratuities are not included. Tips are not included in tour costs.
programs.cancellation_note: Cancel by email. With 60 days notice or more you get a full refund less a $50 admin fee per person. With 31 to 59 days notice you get half back and the deposit is not refunded. With 30 days or less there is no refund.

programs.name: Robson Bight Kayak Day Tour
programs.description: A full day guided kayak tour from Telegraph Cove to the boundary of the Robson Bight Ecological Reserve, with a 40 minute custom landing craft ride in one direction and two to three hours of paddling in the morning and again in the afternoon. The published rate is $400.00 CAD per person plus tax, and that is the only rate given, so children pay the same as adults. The day runs 8:30 am to 4:30 pm, group size is 4 minimum and 10 maximum, and the meeting point is Bauza Cove, Telegraph Cove. The season is July 1 to September 10. The participation page says it is suitable for children aged 9 and older, and points families with children under 9 to custom trips. Lunch, all paddling and kayak equipment and a certified guide are included.
programs.what_children_do: Meet at the beach at 8:30 in the morning, ride a landing craft for about 40 minutes in one direction, and paddle a kayak for two to three hours in the morning and again in the afternoon along the Johnstone Strait shoreline. They watch for orcas, humpbacks, sea lions, porpoises, seals and eagles, look at sea stars, anemones and nudibranchs in the intertidal zone, and stop for a provided lunch before getting back around 4 in the afternoon.
programs.our_note: Nine is the youngest they take on this one, and the site is blunt that you need to be fit enough for four to five hours of paddling, so it suits an older youth group rather than a class outing. Only ten seats exist per day and four people have to sign up for it to run. If you have children under nine, the site says to ask about a custom trip instead.
programs.practical_summary: Lunch, kayaks and all paddling gear are included, the day is eight hours long and entirely outdoors on the water, and parking is at their Telegraph Cove base. There is nothing on the site about washrooms at the meeting beach, wet weather plans, how many adults have to come, or how far ahead to book, so ask when you call.

programs.name: West Coast Trail guided hike
programs.description: An 8 day, 7 night guided backpacking expedition over the 75 kilometre West Coast Trail, ending with a 4 hour evening tour of Kiixin with the Huu-ay-aht First Nations on day seven. The group is a maximum of 8 guests plus 2 guides. Besides personal clothing and toiletries, each participant carries roughly 12 to 15 kilograms of shared group gear such as food, tents and cooking equipment. Start dates are set each year with Parks Canada; the 2025 season listed August 1 to 7 and August 15 to 21. No price and no minimum age are published anywhere on the site for this trip, and the only route to book it is the form on its dates page.
programs.our_note: This is a 75 kilometre backpacking expedition over eight days, with ladder systems, tide timings and a 12 to 15 kilogram pack each. The site gives it no price and no youngest age, and its own description says most guests come away exhausted. It is not a trip for a children's group.
programs.practical_summary: Only the group size, the length and the packing weight are published. There is no price, no youngest age and no start date beyond last season's two, so anything practical would have to come from a phone call.
programs.evidence: We have a maximum of 8 guests plus 2 guides.

gaps: no school, daycare or youth group rate is published anywhere; the home page twice says to ask about group discounts but never gives a number or a condition
the youngest age differs by trip: the 4 day camp takes children from 8, the one day kayak tour says 9 and older, and families with children under 9 are pointed to unpriced custom trips
no minimum age at all is published for the West Coast Trail hike
no price is published for the West Coast Trail hike, and its months are unknown; the only dates shown are two August departures from the 2025 season
the day tour publishes one flat rate of $400 per person plus tax; no separate child rate is published, so the per-child figure recorded is that same flat rate
the amount of the deposit and when the balance is due are not published for any trip; the deposit is only mentioned inside the cancellation policy
no lead time or minimum notice for booking is published for any trip
no adult supervision ratio is published for children on any trip
washrooms at the Telegraph Cove meeting beach are not mentioned; the only toilet described is the composting system out at the remote camp
wheelchair and stroller access are not addressed anywhere on the site
no wet weather alternative is described; the site only says extended rain is unusual but possible
bus parking is not addressed; the site says car parking at the base is included with the camp tour
prices carry no year label, but the departure lists on the camp and West Coast Trail pages are both headed 2025, so the rates may be a season out of date
the site publishes a map pin for Orca Camp at Warden Beach, roughly 14 km southeast of the Telegraph Cove address, which is the remote camp rather than the place a group arrives at

most photographs on the site carry an empty alt attribute, so only the two images that have real alt text of their own were recorded; the day tour and camp banner photos were left out rather than described unseen
